overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of Merleau-Ponty's late self-critique. You'll be asked about the self-critique, the tacit cogito, hyper-reflection, the critiques of reflection and intuition, and the status of the working notes.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

forms.stemHtml: Why did Merleau-Ponty come to judge the problems of Phenomenology of Perception insoluble?

options.html: Because it relied on empirical evidence that was later disproved
options.text: Because it relied on empirical evidence that was later disproved
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The problem he identifies is the book's starting point, not its evidence.

options.html: Because it started from the consciousness–object distinction
options.text: Because it started from the consciousness–object distinction
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Starting there, every link between subject and world had to bridge a gap the starting point opened.

options.html: Because it claimed that mind and body are separate substances
options.text: Because it claimed that mind and body are separate substances
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The book argued against that. The problem is its starting point, not an explicit claim.

options.html: Because it ignored the body in favor of pure consciousness
options.text: Because it ignored the body in favor of pure consciousness
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The book was centered on the body. The problem is its consciousness–object starting point.

forms.stemHtml: What was the tacit cogito, and what did Merleau-Ponty later conclude about it?

options.html: Descartes's explicit "I think," which he later defended
options.text: Descartes's explicit "I think," which he later defended
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The tacit cogito was meant to lie beneath the explicit cogito. He later judged it impossible.

options.html: A silent self-presence, later judged impossible
options.text: A silent self-presence, later judged impossible
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Removing it removed the last foundation of the philosophy of consciousness.

options.html: A method of reflection, later replaced by intuition
options.text: A method of reflection, later replaced by intuition
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The tacit cogito was a silent self-presence, not a method.

options.html: A theory of language, later extended to painting
options.text: A theory of language, later extended to painting
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The tacit cogito was a silent self-presence beneath reflection and speech.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following describe how to read the working notes of The Visible and the Invisible? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Treat them as provisional, not final doctrine
options.text: Treat them as provisional, not final doctrine
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Merleau-Ponty wrote them to think, not to publish.

options.html: Read each note alongside related notes and the chapters
options.text: Read each note alongside related notes and the chapters
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A single note is evidence of a line of thought.

options.html: Expect compression, abbreviations, and missing context
options.text: Expect compression, abbreviations, and missing context
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Many notes are lists of phrases and questions.

options.html: Assume every note is consistent with every other
options.text: Assume every note is consistent with every other
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Different notes sometimes pull in different directions.

options.html: Treat the notes as edited and approved by Merleau-Ponty
options.text: Treat the notes as edited and approved by Merleau-Ponty
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. They were edited by Claude Lefort after Merleau-Ponty's death.

forms.stemHtml: What is Merleau-Ponty's term, translating surréflexion, for a reflection that takes account of its own roots in unreflected experience and of the changes it makes to what it reflects on? Enter one word (use a hyphen if needed).

options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Hyper-reflection describes from within, knowing it does.
Correct! Hyper-reflection describes from within, knowing it does.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Merleau-Ponty calls this hyper-reflection.

forms.stemHtml: Why does Merleau-Ponty find philosophies of intuition, such as Bergson's, wanting?

options.html: Because they rely too heavily on scientific measurement
options.text: Because they rely too heavily on scientific measurement
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. His objection is to the goal of coinciding with things.

options.html: Because they deny that perception gives us anything at all
options.text: Because they deny that perception gives us anything at all
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. His objection is that they seek a fusion with things that never comes.

options.html: Because they seek a coincidence with things that never comes
options.text: Because they seek a coincidence with things that never comes
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! There is always a gap, and at most a partial coincidence.

options.html: Because they begin from a pure nothingness opposed to being
options.text: Because they begin from a pure nothingness opposed to being
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. That's his objection to dialectic. Intuition seeks coincidence.

title: The Self-Critique
